summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload disguised as a trivial test package
details: The package advertises itself as a monorepo test package whose entire declared functionality is `export default 'John';` in lib/index.js. Its package.json preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which is variable-name-obfuscated (hex identifiers) and downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip` into a temp directory, extracts the platform-appropriate `bun` binary, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle using obfuscator.io-style rotated-string-array control-flow obfuscation (shuffle function, large numeric constant table, hex-named globals) with no relationship to the advertised one-line string export. On `npm install`, this executes an opaque, heavily obfuscated payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime that bypasses Node-focused install-time inspection. The mismatch between the trivial advertised purpose and the shipped dropper+payload, combined with obfuscation of both the loader and the executed bundle, is the alternate-runtime-dropper attack shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
